properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Raised by an external agent-side field report, 2026-08-11 (fact:external-agent-side-report-2026-08-11, redacted).

WHAT THEY OBSERVED. Several of their acknowledgements carried explicit retirement conditions written into the reason — of the shape "revisit when the first implementation exists", "replace this when that work is scheduled". One of those conditions had been true for weeks and nothing surfaced it. `reviewed_gaps` says an acknowledgement is "worth re-reading when the design shifts" and nothing detects the shift. Their line: acknowledgements are where gaps go to be forgotten SAFELY, and the safety decays silently.

⚠️ NARROWER THAN THEY WROTE, AND THE NARROWING IS THE POINT. Expiry machinery EXISTS: a review expires when the set of nodes it judged changes, and `req:set-scoped-acknowledgement-keys-on-its-rule` (accepted) already fixed the case where a set-scoped acknowledgement expired merely because the design grew. So this is NOT "acknowledgements never expire". It is that the trigger is always the same trigger — the affected set moved — and a human-stated condition ("when an artifact of this kind first appears") is invisible to it. Recording the narrow version matters, because the wide version reads as a defect in something that works.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) A typed re-review trigger on the acknowledgement: a node type appearing, a count crossing zero, an edge arriving. Expressive, and it is a small query language nobody asked for — every one of those is a new thing to specify, validate and explain.
(b) No new vocabulary: have `loop_status` flag acknowledgements older than N design-changes as re-review candidates. Crude, cheap, and it needs no condition to be stated correctly at write time — which matters, because the person acknowledging a gap is the least likely to predict what would falsify it.
(c) Let the acknowledgement name the NODE TYPE it is waiting on, and nothing more. Covers the reported case exactly ("when the first artifact exists") at a fraction of (a)'s cost.
(d) Nothing. `req:review-expires-when-what-it-judged-changes` is already proposed and unbuilt; finish that before adding a second expiry axis beside it.

⚠️ THE TRAP: a stated condition that is WRONG is worse than no condition, because it reads as watched. An acknowledgement saying "revisit when X" that nothing evaluates is the same false-assurance shape as a `planned` verification silencing a gap — which this project already refuses. Whatever is offered must actually be evaluated, or must not be offered.

📌 SITS BESIDE `req:review-expires-when-what-it-judged-changes` (proposed): that one is about the trigger being too NARROW (only the set, not the content). This is about the trigger being SINGULAR. Same subsystem, different complaint, and they should be read together.
properties.name: OPEN — should an acknowledged gap be able to declare a machine-checkable re-review trigger, rather than stating its retirement condition in prose?
properties.rationale: A real acknowledgement carried a condition that came true and nothing noticed. But expiry machinery exists and works on a different trigger, so the honest finding is that the trigger is singular rather than absent — and a stated-but-unevaluated condition would be a worse failure than the current silence, because it would read as watched.
